subject: Heliogen VPC surge: p95 latency & 502s — ops playbook
messages:
From: Samir Patel <ops@heliogen.io>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@heliogen.io
Date: 2028-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent — sustained p95 latency and intermittent 502s on our VPC cluster

Hi Dylan / Laura,

We're seeing a persistent p95 latency regression (from ~220ms to ~1.6s) and intermittent 502s across our private VPC serving cluster starting ~02:30 UTC this morning. Traffic pattern is our normal daytime traffic (no spike > 1.2x) but errors are highest on long-sequence generation requests and batch overflow seems correlated.

Initial observations from our side:
- Queue depth on inference nodes increased steadily before errors (avg queue 25 -> 110).
- Memory pressure spikes on worker-03 with OOM-kernel messages in syslog.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~18% for popular prefixes.

Can Redwood run a quick triage and propose immediate mitigations? This is affecting customer-facing SLAs — procurement and our CS team are closely watching.

I've attached a small support bundle with metric excerpts and sample request traces. Happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Samir
Ops Lead, Heliogen
Attachment: heliogen-support-bundle-20280418.tar.gz (log bundle)
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <ops@heliogen.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-18T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent — sustained p95 latency and intermittent 502s on our VPC cluster

Samir — thanks for the heads up and the bundle. We're on it.

Immediate triage plan (next 60m):
1) Gather live metrics from your control plane (queue lengths, host-level mem/cpu, kernel logs).
2) Temporarily reduce max_concurrency on the route serving long-sequence requests to 4 to limit queue buildup.
3) Enable aggressive prefix-level KV cache (increase table size + eviction TTL) to recover hit-rate.
4) If a node shows repeated OOMs, we will cordon + restart worker processes one at a time to avoid cascade.

I'm looping in Vivek (serving runtime) and Laura (CS lead) to lead execution. Please confirm a 30-minute maintenance window for rolling restarts if we need to.

- Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Patel <ops@heliogen.io>
Date: 2028-04-18T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent — Urgent triage plan for Heliogen VPC

On Tue, Apr 18, 2028 at 09:35 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I'm looping in Vivek (serving runtime) and Laura (CS lead) to lead execution.

Thanks — quick notes from runtime side after a fast scan of the bundle and metrics:
- The symptoms point to KV cache churn + load imbalanced by request length distribution (large sequences filling worker queues).
- Our prior similar incidents were resolved by a combination of: limiting concurrency for long-seq routes, enabling soft-batching (lower max_batch_size), and temporarily falling back to the quantized model variant for heavy decode paths.

Immediate actions I'm going to execute with your approval:
A) Set route config:
   - max_concurrency: 4
   - max_batch_size: 8
   - prefer_quantized: true (fallback only for >1024 tokens)
B) Increase KV cache allocation for prefix table by 40% across the cluster and set eviction_ttl to 18m.
C) Restart worker on host-03 (cordon -> drain -> restart) during the window to clear kernel mem fragmentation.

Estimate: changes A+B in <15m, restart in next 30–45m if window ok. I will monitor p50/p95 and 502 rate and report back.

Attachments: prelim-action-plan.md (actionable steps and rollback)

- Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
From: Samir Patel <ops@heliogen.io>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, procurement@heliogen.io
Date: 2028-04-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent — sustained p95 latency and intermittent 502s on our VPC cluster

Thanks Dylan/Vivek — we approve the maintenance window now. Please proceed with A+B immediately and perform the host restart on host-03 at 10:30 PT.

One note from our infra team: host-03 also runs data-plane transformations (tokenization) for some services — please ensure cold-start impacts are confined to the route in question.

I'll be on the call at 10:25.

Best,
Samir
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <ops@heliogen.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-18T10:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent — sustained p95 latency and intermittent 502s on our VPC cluster

Quick status update (post changes):
- max_concurrency reduced -> immediate drop in queue depth (avg 110 -> 27).
- KV cache hit-rate recovered to +12% vs baseline after raising allocation.
- 502s have dropped from 72/hr -> 3/hr; p95 improved from 1.6s -> 380ms for affected routes.
- host-03 restart completed and warmed (no repeat OOM).

Next actions:
- We'll keep prefer_quantized enabled for the next 12 hours and monitor for quality regressions; CS, please surface any generation anomalies.
- Schedule a deeper post-mortem with kernel/allocator team and propose longer-term tuning (batching profile, kernel selection heuristics).

I'll post the prelim action notes and a link to the deeper investigation doc in the drive.

- Dylan
From: Grace Long <grace.long@heliogen.io>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Patel <ops@heliogen.io>, procurement@heliogen.io, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-20T17:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Helio VPC surge: follow-up and request for exec summary

Dylan — thanks again for the quick action. The immediate impact reduction looked good and our CS reported no material quality regressions for customer traffic.

Procurement wants an executive summary for our account team (high-level cause, actions taken, expected recurrence risk, and any credits). Could you provide a 1-page exec summary and include proposed follow-up items (timeline for permanent kernel tuning and a recommended periodic KV sizing review)?

Also looping in procurement to start a ticket for SLA credit based on the error window.

Thanks,
Grace Long
Head of Platform Ops — Heliogen
